standard_prerequisites.use: Makes d_0 d_2 = d_1 d_0 and d_1 d_2 = d_1 d_1 meaningful for the displayed isomorphisms.

standard_prerequisites.use: The target notion (monomorphism j, transitivity, reflexivity, symmetry) verified in the proof.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 6798-6809): for a cartesian morphism pi : Y -> (X/S)_bullet of simplicial schemes, j = (d^1_1, d^1_0) : Y_1 -> Y_0 x_S Y_0 defines an equivalence relation on Y_0 over S.
Monomorphism (proof lines 6811-6815): the composition Y_1 -> Y_0 x_S Y_0 -> Y_0 x_S X is an isomorphism because pi is cartesian, so j is a monomorphism.

Transitivity (lines 6817-6841): the morphism (d^2_2, d^2_0) : Y_2 -> Y_1 x_{d^1_0, Y_0, d^1_1} Y_1 is well-defined by the simplicial identity d_0 d_2 = d_1 d_0 and is an isomorphism by cartesianness; combined with d^2_1 : Y_2 -> Y_1 it yields the composition morphism c : Y_1 x_{s,Y_0,t} Y_1 -> Y_1 over Y_0 x_S Y_0, which immediately gives transitivity of Y_1(T) subset Y_0(T) x Y_0(T) for every T/S.

Reflexivity and symmetry (lines 6843-6872): reflexivity follows because the restriction of j to the diagonal Delta : X -> X x_S X is an isomorphism (cartesianness); symmetry uses the isomorphism (d^2_2, d^2_1) : Y_2 -> Y_1 x_{d^1_1, Y_0, d^1_1} Y_1 (well-defined by d_1 d_2 = d_1 d_1, iso by cartesianness), which gives: if a ~ b and a ~ c then b ~ c, and with reflexivity this yields the symmetric inverse, completing the equivalence relation.
proof_roadmap: Prove j is a monomorphism through the cartesian identification with Y_0 x_S X.
Build the composition morphism from the (d^2_2, d^2_0) isomorphism and deduce transitivity.
Deduce reflexivity from the diagonal and symmetry from the (d^2_2, d^2_1) isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: Equivalence-relation lemma (statement 6798-6809, proof 6811-6872): the four defining properties of an equivalence relation are each argued in the span - monomorphism via the cartesian identification, transitivity via the composition morphism built from the (d^2_2, d^2_0) isomorphism, reflexivity via the diagonal, symmetry via the (d^2_2, d^2_1) isomorphism; the two 'Details omitted.' passages are auxiliary fibre-product rewirings whose cause (cartesianness of pi) is named and one instance displayed. H2.
